title: open-model-signal-framework
content:
Purpose:
This is a working messaging + competitive brief for how we position the Redwood model catalog when selling open-source and community models. Instead of only surfacing raw benchmarks or model names, the approach centers on observable signals and operational compatibility — a repeatable framework sales, product marketing, and docs can use to explain model selection, tradeoffs, and confidence for production use.

Objectives (what success looks like):
- A succinct narrative that helps engineers and buying teams choose models for three common product intents: low-latency chat, high-precision generation, and dense-embedding search.
- A one-page sales / solutions checklist that reduces discovery time by 30% (fewer back-and-forths to verify fit).
- Differentiation versus cloud-managed model endpoints and DIY inference runtimes: focus on production signals, runtime compatibility, and predictable economics.

Core idea (executive summary):
Users care about two things: output quality on their tasks, and predictable cost/latency when serving. For open models, we bridge the gap by exposing a set of curated "model signals" (observable, testable characteristics) and attaching standardized compatibility badges (runtime-tested, security/PKG checks, quantization profiles). The catalog becomes a tool for evidence-driven selection: match workload signals -> recommended quality band -> deployment recipe.

Model Signals (the building blocks):
- Task fidelity: measured by task-specific evals (customizable) — examples: instruction-following score, summarization ROUGE-like aggregate, retrieval-augmented generation F1.
- Latency per-token (median and p95) on common instance classes and sequence lengths.
- Memory/kv-cache behavior: long-context friendliness, memory growth per token, cache reuse efficiency for chat workloads.
- Quantization robustness: perceived quality delta for int8/q4 variants (numeric banding).
- Determinism / variance: distribution of outputs over repeated prompts (important for ranking/rerank tasks).
- Safety surface: baseline toxicity/PII leakage heuristics on standard probe sets.
- Cost signal: tokens-to-complete metrics under representative prompts mapped to cloud instance costs.

Quality Bands and Compatibility Tiers (minimal taxonomy):
- Band A — Production-grade, low rework: high task fidelity on core benchmarks, p95 latency < target, quantization-friendly presets, safety pass.
- Band B — Prototype-to-scale: good fidelity with expected tuning, moderate latency; recommended for customer-hosted pilots.
- Band C — Exploratory / research: strong capabilities in narrow tasks or SOTA research models but limited production guarantees.

Compatibility tiers (runtime badges):
- Runtime-Verified: the model has passed our serving runtime smoke tests for inference correctness, KV cache behavior, and streaming output.
- Quantized-Ready: validated quantized artifact and documented quality deltas.
- Tiered-Fallback Compatible: modeled for graceful fallback to cheaper variants when capacity constrained.

How this maps to buyer personas:
- Platform Engineers: focus on compatibility badges, latency/cost signals, and autoscaling recipes. Provide a short "integration recipe" that maps model -> instance class -> batching config.
- ML Engineers: focus on task fidelity and quantization robustness; provide eval sets, example prompts, and per-model tuning notes.
- Product Managers / PMMs: focus on user-facing failure modes, quality bands, and SLAs to cite in feature specs.

Messaging principles (short):
1) Evidence-first: surface the most relevant signals for the buyer's intent up-front.
2) Actionable next steps: pairing model suggestions with a one-click test-run and a deployment recipe.
3) Tradeoff clarity: present quality vs cost vs latency as explicit knobs not buried in docs.
4) Safety & lineage: make provenance and safety probes visible to reduce enterprise friction.

Sales/Field play (one-pager content to hand to sellers):
- Opening line: "Pick the model that meets your intent — not just the most-starred repo. Our catalog maps models to signals and gives you a tested deployment recipe."
- Qualification questions (to speed discovery): target intent (chat vs search vs generation), expected QPS and p95 latency target, tolerance for quantization quality loss, regulatory/data residency constraints.
- Quick recommend flows: If low-latency chat + strict p95 -> show Band A Runtime-Verified models with instance recipes; If high-fidelity long-doc summarization -> show Band A/B models with context-extension notes; If embeddings at scale -> present quantized-ready models with batching profiles and expected cost per 1M vectors.
- Objection handling: "Why not just pick the largest model?" -> Largest != best: platform signals like cold-start latency, KV cache efficiency, and quantization sensitivity drive real costs. Offer a pilot comparison report.

Competitive overview (high level takeaways):
- HypotheticalCompetitor A (cloud-managed endpoints): Sells simplicity: model selection is opaque and benchmarked on a small set of workloads. Our edge: we expose per-use-case signals, and provide runtime-tested compatibility so customers can predict production costs.
- HypotheticalCompetitor B (self-hosted runtime vendors): Offers flexible stack but leaves model vetting to customers. Our edge: we couple runtime with curated open-model evidence and pre-built deployment recipes, reducing time-to-safe-production.

Proof assets to build (priority):
1) "Model signal cards" — compact one-pagers per model showing 6 signals, recommended use cases, and recipe to reproduce tests.
2) A short interactive demo that lets customers toggle intents and shows recommended models + cost/latency estimates.
3) A 2-slide sales battle card that summarizes differentiators vs cloud-managed endpoints and DIY runtimes.

Launch timeline (minimal):
- Week 0–2: finalize signal schema and coverage for top 12 open models.
- Week 3: create model signal cards and sales battle card.
- Week 4: internal beta with solutions engineers + 3 pilot accounts.
- Week 6: public catalog update + blog + demo.

Metrics to watch post-launch:
- Reduction in model-selection support tickets (target 40% less in month 1).
- Conversion lift on trials that use catalog recommendations vs those that don’t.
- Time-to-first-successful-deploy metric for pilot customers.

Open questions / risks:
- How many evals are needed per signal to be persuasive without over-indexing on narrow benchmarks? Suggested approach: start with one standardized probe per signal and leave room for customer-provided evals.
- Legal/brand risk of surfacing community models with controversial outputs. Mitigation: safety surface + provenance + optional opt-out for enterprise catalogs.
- Engineering cost to maintain "runtime-verified" badge across model updates and new releases. Consider automation for smoke tests in CI.

Immediate next steps (owner: Priya with ENG + ML support):
- Align on 12 initial models and finalize the signal schema (deadline: 2025-10-15).
- Draft the first 6 model cards and a sample integration recipe (deadline: 2025-10-30).
- Sync with Solutions Eng for pilot candidates (Evan to own outreach).

Notes to reviewers:
This doc is intentionally practical and commercialization-focused. Looking for feedback from SOLENG and ML infra on: which signals are most realistic to compute at scale, and how often we should re-run smoke tests to keep the compatibility badges up to date.

End.
